status: PROPOSAL - research data only. This file is NOT authoritative simulation state and NOT renderer presentation data. It does not finalise a runtime schema. Canonical settlement/location identities (RFC 4122 UUIDv5, ADR-0009) are minted only by the atlas pipeline at integration time; the proposedId values here are research handles, not canonical IDs.
subject: R-16 historical settlement roster, first batch (batch 1)
envelopeRegion: 1 - Italy, Sicily & the islands (incl. Cisalpine Gaul)
batchScope: Italy, Sicily, Sardinia, Corsica, Magna Graecia and the surrounding central Mediterranean
coordinateConvention: WGS84 decimal degrees, approximate representative points for the ancient site (not the modern town unless noted). Precision does not imply archaeological accuracy and is not a surveyed building location.
idScheme: proposedId = r16-ita-<slug>; the slug (key) is region-scoped to avoid homonyms (e.g. Neapolis in Campania vs Sardinia). Stable, human-readable, non-canonical.
methodNote: Records are compiled from independent evidence (primary literary/administrative sources, archaeology and the Pleiades gazetteer for coordinates). Game/mod faction names are discovery leads only and never authorities. Every coordinate is a representative point with an explicit location confidence; where only a broad location is known the coordinate is coarse or null. Political authority is recorded only where supported; otherwise it is left unclaimed.
sourceAuditNote: Pleiades gazetteer identifiers are recorded only as 'to be confirmed', never asserted: automated access to pleiades.stoa.org was blocked by the site's anti-scraping protection during this pass, so no Pleiades id has been verified. Coordinates are approximate representative points, not surveyed locations or building footprints. All literary sources (Polybius, Livy, Diodorus, Strabo, Pliny, Pausanias, Ptolemy) are later than 278 BCE and are dated in each record; they are evidence for continuity, not contemporary snapshots. Confirming Pleiades ids and site coordinates manually remains an integration prerequisite.
duplicateGuard: None of these records reproduce the 23 active atlas sites (roma, capua, tibur, praeneste, norba, tarracina, ostia, antium, lanuvium, aricia, anagnia, fregellae, arpinum, setia, formiae, minturnae, cumae, neapolis, nola, pompeii, maleventum, poseidonia, diana-nemi), the 12 deferred candidates (Lavinium, Cora, Fidenae, Taras, Brentesion, Venusia, Luceria, Elea, Rhegion, Herakleia, Thourioi, Taurasia) or the excluded site (Cosa).

records.existenceEvidence: One of the foremost Etruscan cities, continuously occupied from the Villanovan period through the campaign; the port at Graviscae and the great chamber-tomb necropoleis document an unbroken urban tradition.
records.politicalAuthority: Etruscan city, a Roman ally/subject after the Roman victories of 283; the Etruscan league is defunct.
records.architectureContext: Etruscan tufa ashlar fortifications and terraced walls over a tufa plateau, podium temples, and chamber-tomb necropoleis below the city; the coastal emporion of Graviscae carries the port function.
chronologyNotes: Occupied through the 3rd c. BCE; no founding discontinuity at the campaign date.
Roman hegemony follows the defeat of the Etruscan cities in the 280s.
anachronismWarnings: Do not depict the Etruscan league as an independent polity at 278.
Do not use later Roman imperial monumentality as the city's chronology.
sources: Livy, Ab Urbe Condita (Etruscan campaigns, books 9-10)
Pleiades gazetteer (CC BY 3.0; record id to be confirmed)
Barrington Atlas of the Greek and Roman World, map 42
unresolved: Precise legal status (socius vs subject) in 278.
Ancient shoreline and the Graviscae port extent.

records.existenceEvidence: A major Etruscan city with a continuous archaeological sequence; it had received Roman civitas sine suffragio in 353, so it was already inside the Roman civic system before the campaign.
records.politicalAuthority: Roman civitas sine suffragio (semi-citizen community with Roman obligations but restricted franchise).
records.architectureContext: Etruscan tumulus necropolis (Banditaccia) beside a tufa plateau city; the coastal sanctuaries and ports of Pyrgi and Alsium carry the maritime function.
chronologyNotes: Civitas sine suffragio in 353; inside the Roman system at the campaign date.
anachronismWarnings: Do not show a later Roman municipal re-plan as the campaign-era city.
sources: Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)
unresolved: Extent of the city and its dependent ports at 278.

records.existenceEvidence: A major Etruscan city of the classical period; it submitted to Rome after the 280s and was already in decline. The city is still inhabited at the campaign date, but on a reduced footing.
records.politicalAuthority: Etruscan city under Roman control after the campaigns of the 280s.
records.architectureContext: Tufa plateau city with Etruscan walls, temples and rich chamber tombs; in relative decline relative to the 6th-5th c. peak.
chronologyNotes: Roman victory over Vulci in 280; the neighbouring Latin colony at Cosa follows in 273 - after the campaign date.
anachronismWarnings: Do not depict Cosa (273 BCE) as existing.
Do not show the city at its archaic peak.
sources: Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)
unresolved: Whether the city itself remained a functioning political centre or only a residual town in 278.

coordinates.precision: approximate representative point (Orvieto; identity of the 278 site is discussed)

records.existenceEvidence: A leading Etruscan community and a candidate seat of the federal sanctuary (Fanum Voltumnae); its revolt and Roman destruction belong to 264, so at 278 the Etruscan city still stands.
records.politicalAuthority: Etruscan city under Roman hegemony; restive inside the Roman alliance system.
records.architectureContext: Hilltop tufa city; the federal sanctuary of Voltumna is associated with the Volsinian territory.
chronologyNotes: Etruscan city in 278; Roman destruction and refoundation as Volsinii Novi follow in 264.
The identification of the 278 city with Orvieto is the prevailing but not settled view.
anachronismWarnings: Do not use Volsinii Novi (Bolsena) as the 278 site.
Do not show the 264 destruction as already happened.
sources: Livy, Ab Urbe Condita (264 BCE Volsinii episode)
Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)
unresolved: Identity and precise location of the 278 settlement relative to the 264 refoundation.
Whether the Fanum Voltumnae sat in this territory at the campaign date.

records.existenceEvidence: A major inland Etruscan city allied to Rome during the Third Samnite War; its continued occupation through the 3rd c. is well attested.
records.politicalAuthority: Etruscan city, a Roman ally/socius.
records.architectureContext: Etruscan circuit walls and gates over a commanding hill; a major craft and agricultural centre of the Arno/Chiana corridor.
chronologyNotes: Allied to Rome by 295; no discontinuity at the campaign date.
anachronismWarnings: Do not use the later Arretine sigillata pottery industry as a campaign-era marker (it flourishes from the 1st c. BCE).
sources: Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)

records.existenceEvidence: The principal Etruscan coastal city and metallurgical harbour, facing the iron-bearing island of Ilva (Elba); its industrial activity continued into the Roman period.
records.politicalAuthority: Etruscan city under Roman hegemony after the 280s.
records.architectureContext: Etruscan walls and gates on the promontory, tumulus and chamber tombs, and extensive iron-working slag deposits tied to the Elba ore trade.
chronologyNotes: Continuous occupation; iron/metallurgy is a defining 278 BCE function.
anachronismWarnings: Do not present the later Roman harbour works as campaign-era.
sources: Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)
unresolved: Ancient shoreline and the relationship of the city to its ports.

records.existenceEvidence: A major Etruscan hill city, incorporated into the Roman alliance system by the early 3rd c. and continuously occupied.
records.politicalAuthority: Etruscan city, a Roman ally/socius.
records.architectureContext: One of the largest Etruscan circuit walls with the Porta all'Arco gate; a commanding hilltop over the Cecina valley.
chronologyNotes: Roman alliance by the early 3rd c.; no discontinuity at the campaign date.
anachronismWarnings: Do not use later Roman urbanization as the campaign-era city.
sources: Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)

records.existenceEvidence: A principal Umbrian community, later famous for the Iguvine Tables which record its civic and religious institutions; occupation through the 3rd c. is attested.
records.politicalAuthority: Umbrian city (Roman ally/socius).
records.architectureContext: Hill-foot Umbrian town with an associated sanctuary on the slopes of Monte Ingino; the Iguvine Tables document a collegium of Augural/priestly officials and ritual processions.
chronologyNotes: The surviving Tables are 2nd-1st c. BCE but encode institutional practice relevant to the Umbrian community.
anachronismWarnings: Do not date the bronze tables themselves to 278; use them only as institutional evidence with caution.
sources: Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)
unresolved: Precise 278 political status.

records.existenceEvidence: An existing Umbrian settlement on a strategic Apennine spur. Its Latin colony dates to 241, so at the campaign date it is a native community, not a colony.
records.politicalAuthority: Umbrian settlement under Roman hegemony (not yet a Latin colony).
records.architectureContext: Hill-controlled settlement commanding the route north through the Apennines.
chronologyNotes: Latin colony only in 241 BCE - after the campaign date.
anachronismWarnings: Do NOT show Spoletium as a Latin colony at 278; the colony is 241 BCE.
sources: Pleiades gazetteer (record id to be confirmed)
unresolved: Name and status of the pre-colonial settlement.

records.architectureContext: Harbour town on a promontory with a Greek colonial urban tradition.
